product.name: CredMgr
product.summary: A local, offline credential vault for macOS. Secrets are organised into nodes (projects); every access decision is made by one local process, the broker (credmgrd). The desktop app, the command line and the MCP server are all clients of it.
product.network: No network listener and no outbound connection.

release_state: 2.0.0-beta.1 is published as an unsigned GitHub pre-release (2026-11-01); this tree is 2.0.0-rc.2, built locally and unsigned, not published. Unsigned and not notarised until a Developer ID is applied. On a Mac with a Secure Enclave, Touch ID and device unlock are available; the passphrase stays the root of trust everywhere else.

how_to_use_this_file: You are an AI agent (or you are configuring one) that works with a CredMgr vault. Read safety_model and never first.
Use only the MCP tools in mcp_tools. Do not talk to the broker socket, read the vault folder, run credmgr unlock, or ask the user for their passphrase, recovery code or authenticator code.
Start with credmgr_whoami, then use how_to_read and how_to_write for the task.
When a result is an error, find its code in error_codes and do what it says. Refusals are explicit: tell the operator what you need, in one sentence, and carry on with other work.
features describes everything the product can do for a human, where it is, and (agent_access) what an agent may do with it. Anything with status 'planned' does not exist yet; do not rely on it.

safety_model.values_stay_in_the_broker: Secret values are encrypted at rest and decrypted only inside the broker. A value leaves the broker only as the answer to one identified, authorised, logged request. The product makes no outbound network connection, so a value cannot be sent anywhere by CredMgr itself.
safety_model.one_enforcement_point: The broker (credmgrd) decides every access. The desktop app, the CLI and the MCP server are thin clients; none holds a key and none can widen what the broker allows. An MCP tool forwards its arguments to one broker operation unchanged.
safety_model.agent_scope: An agent token is scoped to exactly one node, resolved from the folder the agent was started in (the node's work folders) or from an explicit token fixed when it was issued. The agent reads that node, its ancestors and Global. It reads its descendants only if the node's policy sets descendant-read, and a sibling only for sub-nodes whose parent shares them; both widenings need a human and, in this build, a presence check that cannot be given. Projects never read each other. No tool argument changes any of this.

agent_access_levels.note: Set per node by a human (node policy). The notes and admin capabilities are never part of an agent's scope.

sensitive_reveals_wait_for_a_human: If the whole vault is locked, a request for a value is recorded and answered approval_pending. A person decides it with the passphrase (and the authenticator code when two-factor is on) on the Lock screen or with `credmgr approve`; approval covers one request, one entry, once, and expires after 120 seconds. The vault stays locked.

If the node's policy requires a second factor (reveal or always) and the vault has one enrolled, an agent gets two_factor_required until a person proves the factor. One code opens a vault-wide window of five minutes. The owner's own login is not asked.
A value is never staged for one caller and handed to another: an approval is one slot per (node, entry, requester) and releases only the fields that request asked for.

writes.create_while_locked: credmgr_create works on a locked vault. The entry is not written to the manifest: it is held in a review tray and a person accepts or discards it. Say so to the operator.
writes.update_needs_unlocked: credmgr_update, credmgr_rotate, credmgr_remove, credmgr_undo and the three field tools need the vault and node unlocked, because overwriting a credential you cannot read would be credential substitution.
writes.generation_check: Every change to an existing entry carries its current generation. A concurrent change answers conflict; re-read and retry once.
writes.undo: Rotations, field changes and removals are undoable by audit record id. A removal and a field change can be undone for seven days; a rotation has no time limit. Undo is itself audited.

safety_model.audit: Every decision, allowed or denied, is recorded in a hash-chained log. An agent can read only a redacted feed (id, action, time, actor), never values or before/after content.
safety_model.denials_are_explicit: A refusal names the rule and a remedy that is a human action. The correct response is to ask the human, never to retry, rephrase or look for another route.
safety_model.values_in_your_context: Anything you read with credmgr_get is now in your context. Do not print it into chat, logs, commit messages, files or command arguments; pass it to the program that needs it and nowhere else.
known_limits: Software keystore tier: a copy of the vault folder can be attacked offline with the passphrase; two-factor guards the door (the broker), not the encryption.
A login exported into a shell that an agent also runs in gives that agent every project (known risk K-6). Agents should use the MCP server, never a token.
No presence check exists in this build; everything that needs one is refused for every caller.

human_in_the_loop: Unlocking the vault, approving a waiting request, giving a second-factor code, creating grants, changing node policy or work folders, sealing and restoring nodes, backup, verify and doctor are human actions.
Entries an agent creates while the vault is locked wait for human review before they exist.
A human decides every approval_pending and every two_factor_required.
Anything marked human only in features.agent_access, and every operation with agent_reach 'human_only' in broker_ops, has no agent path.

in_plain_terms: Create or change a grant (a grant is how a human lets one node see into another).
Read the Orphaned node (sealed data). It is absent from the tools, not merely gated.
Read a TOTP seed. credmgr_totp_code gives the current six digits only.
Change a node's policy or agent access, rename a node, re-parent a node, or change its work folders. An agent may not widen its own scope.
List nodes outside its scope. credmgr_whoami names only reachable nodes.
Purge or shorten the audit log, or shorten the seven-day recovery windows.
Read across nodes by any parameter: there is no node override, no 'all', no 'include inherited'.
Reach raw envelopes, keys or file paths.
Run vault-wide maintenance: verify, doctor, backup.
Enrol, replace or recover the vault's second factor.
Turn the machine lock on or off, or read its state.

never: Never create, change or request a grant on your own; ask the operator.
Never try to read another node, the Orphaned node, a node's notes, a TOTP seed, or the vault folder on disk.
Never change a node's policy, agent access, name, parent or work folders, or try to widen your own scope.
Never run backup, verify, doctor, root-key rotation or any second-factor enrolment or recovery.
Never purge or shorten the audit log or a recovery window.
Never call the broker socket or the credmgr command line to get around a refusal; the MCP tools are your whole interface.
Never ask the user for their passphrase, recovery code, recovery codes or authenticator code, and never put them in a command.
Never export or reuse a CREDMGR_TOKEN login.
Never retry a refused or approval_pending request in a loop, rephrase it, or look for another route.
Never print a secret into chat, a log, a commit, a comment or a file, and never pass one as a command-line argument.
Never invent a secret or put a placeholder in code; say exactly which credential is missing and what it is for.
Never describe a feature with status 'planned' or 'partial' as working.

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_whoami
mcp_tools.description: Returns your own node, capabilities, the nodes you can reach, and the node's security level (open, guarded or strict, which is stored as sealed: how much of what you ask for waits for the operator's approval). Call this first and reason about your own boundary instead of discovering it by being denied — it names only nodes you can actually reach, nothing else. You are scoped to one node (resolved from your working directory). You can read that node, its ancestors, Global, and anything explicitly granted. You cannot reach other nodes, and no argument to any tool changes that — if you need something outside your scope, say so and ask the operator.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_list
mcp_tools.description: Lists entry names and metadata (no values) on a node. Scope-filtered — never returns another node's entries.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_search
mcp_tools.description: Searches entry names within your scope. Scope-filtered; a query that only matches outside your scope returns zero results, indistinguishable from a query that matches nothing at all.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_get
mcp_tools.description: Reveals an entry's values. The answer carries `fields` (id, label, value, type, masked for each) and, when exactly one field is returned, `value`. Pass `fieldIds` to reveal only some fields. Subject to the node's two-factor policy, to the vault's lock state and to the node's security level: on a guarded node a high or critical value, and on a strict node every value, answers approval_pending until the operator approves it.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_get_metadata
mcp_tools.description: Describes one entry without revealing it: its type, sensitivity, generation and each field's id, label, type and masking — never a value. Use it to find the field ids the other tools take. Needs the vault and node unlocked (labels are encrypted with the values).
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_create
mcp_tools.description: Creates a new entry (a name not already present on the node): one `value`, or a `fields` array of {label, value} objects for several fields. Send structure — the broker does not parse `label: value` text. Works on a locked vault — lands in the pending tray for human review at next unlock.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_update
mcp_tools.description: Modifies an existing entry: `value` replaces one field's value (name the field with `field` when the entry has several), `fields` replaces the whole list. Requires the vault unlocked — a locked-vault write-without-read-first would be credential substitution, not an update.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_rotate
mcp_tools.description: Replaces an entry's value (or its fields) and preserves the previous ciphertext as history. Takes the same body as credmgr_update. Requires the vault unlocked — same policy gate as credmgr_update: a legitimate rotation implies you could have read what you are replacing.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_field_add
mcp_tools.description: Adds fields to an entry (appended, or inserted at `position`) — it never replaces what is there. The previous state is retained; credmgr_undo reverses it. Requires the vault unlocked.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_field_update
mcp_tools.description: Changes one field — its label, its value, its type or its masking (`"auto"` goes back to inferring a type or masking). The previous state is retained; credmgr_undo reverses it. Requires the vault unlocked.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_field_remove
mcp_tools.description: Removes one field from an entry; the last field cannot be removed (remove the entry instead). The previous state is retained; credmgr_undo reverses it. Requires the vault unlocked.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_remove
mcp_tools.description: Soft-deletes an entry into a 7-day recovery window. Requires the vault unlocked. The entry stops appearing in credmgr_list/credmgr_search immediately; a human can recover it within the window.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_undo
mcp_tools.description: Undoes a rotate, a field change or a removal, addressed by its audit record id (from credmgr_recent_changes) — never by guessing at what changed. Requires the vault unlocked. A removal's undo is only possible within its 7-day recovery window; a rotation's undo has no time limit. This is itself a new, audited action — the original record is never erased or rewritten.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_totp_code
mcp_tools.description: Returns the current 6-digit code for a stored TOTP item. On an entry with several fields, name the seed's field with `field` unless exactly one field is a TOTP seed. Never returns the seed itself — there is no tool that does; a leaked code is worth 30 seconds, a leaked seed is worth forever.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_recent_changes
mcp_tools.description: Redacted feed of recent decisions (allow and deny) — id, action, timestamp, actor. Never before/after values, and never the fields an agent caller cannot have (node, decision, detail): the underlying op is always redacted for an agent origin, not merely by this tool's own choice.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_settings_list
mcp_tools.description: Lists every CredMgr setting with its current value, default, accepted values, what it is for,                 where it is stored, its risk, and the rule for you (`you`): cosmetic and stricter changes apply at once;                 a change that weakens the vault waits for the owner's approval. Pass `node` to include that project's                 settings (only projects you reach).
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_settings_get
mcp_tools.description: Describes one setting in full, with its current value and its recent recorded changes                 (each with the value it replaced and its change id, for credmgr_settings_revert).
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_settings_set
mcp_tools.description: Changes a setting (send the other boolean to toggle). A cosmetic or stricter change applies                 at once and answers `applied: true` with a `changeId`. A change that weakens the vault (a longer or no                 auto-lock, a looser reveal policy, a lower security level, more agent access, screen-capture protection                 off) answers `state: "pending"` with a `request` id: tell the user it waits for their approval in                 CredMgr, then poll credmgr_settings_request. Never retry a pending change in a loop.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_settings_revert
mcp_tools.description: Puts back the value a recorded change replaced, under the same rules as credmgr_settings_set                 (a revert that would weaken the vault waits for the owner).
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_settings_request
mcp_tools.description: The state of a request you made: pending, approved (with the applied change id), denied or                 expired (after 10 minutes). Only the owner approves or denies, in CredMgr on their device.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_kb
mcp_tools.description: The CredMgr knowledge base for language models, as Markdown: every feature, every setting with                 what it is for and where it lives, how to connect, where data is kept, retention and backup, the                 switchboard's rules, and examples. Read it once when you start working with CredMgr.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

error_codes.what_to_do: Stop. The remedy field names the human action that would allow it (usually a grant). Tell the operator what you need and why in one sentence, and carry on with other work. Do not retry or rephrase.

The node asks for a second factor and none is in force. A person must give a code (an elevation lasts five minutes for the whole vault). Ask the operator, then retry once after they confirm. Do not ask for the code yourself.

The vault is locked and the operator has been asked. The request id and the seconds left are in the answer. Wait or do other work; a person decides with the passphrase. Retry the identical request after they say they decided, within 120 seconds. Do not poll in a loop.
Someone changed the entry first. Read it again (credmgr_get_metadata for the new generation), re-apply the change and retry once.
The whole vault is locked. Only entry creation (held for review) is allowed. Do other work or ask the operator to unlock; do not retry in a loop.
The vault is unlocked but this one node is locked. Ask the operator to unlock the node; the remedy field says how.
Not an agent concern: unlock is a human step. Tell the operator.
Fix the request. The message names the problem (an index or field id, never a value). Check the tool's input schema.
Your scope does not carry this capability. Stop and ask the operator; no argument changes it.
No such node, entry, field or request. Check ids with credmgr_list and credmgr_get_metadata.
That name is already used on the node, or is a look-alike of one that is. Choose another name or update the existing entry.
A local failure outside the documented errors. Do not retry in a loop; tell the operator.
This needs a Touch ID check from the vault's owner. An agent cannot give one; tell the operator it is a human action (the app or the CLI asks for the fingerprint itself).
The Touch ID check was missing, expired, already used or did not verify, or Touch ID is not set up. An agent cannot fix it; tell the operator to set up or retry Touch ID.
The seven-day restore window of a sealed node has passed. Terminal; tell the operator.
The operator denied the request, it expired after 120 seconds, or the vault locked after it was approved. Do not retry unprompted; ask the operator whether to ask again.
Too many wrong attempts. retryAfterSeconds says how long to wait. Do not retry in a loop.
A code was wrong, replayed, expired or already used; the broker does not say which. Stop and tell the operator.
No second-factor enrolment is in progress. A human step; tell the operator.
The seven-day recovery window of a removed entry has passed. Terminal.
That audit record cannot be undone (wrong action, denied, or too old). Nothing to do.
A vault already exists. Not an agent concern.
The vault folder is inside a git working tree and is refused. Not an agent concern.
No vault creation is in progress. Not an agent concern.
The retyped recovery code did not match. Not an agent concern.

The vault asks the owner's own login to confirm it is still them (Touch ID or the vault passphrase) before a secret is shown or before that rule is weakened. An agent is never asked this; if you see it, you are holding the owner's login, which you should not. Stop and tell the operator.

The vault's passphrase file is sealed to a Mac whose device key is not here (or it is damaged); 'reason' says which. Unlocking is a human step: tell the operator to open the vault with the recovery code. Not an agent concern; do not retry.
The token presented is not a live login. Do not retry with it. An agent using MCP should not hold a token; tell the operator.

broker_ops.summary: Issue a node-scoped agent token (ADR-164): one node, a subset of what the node allows agents, a mandatory expiry. The owner's login, a fresh second factor where enrolled and a Touch ID proof; the secret is in this answer only.
Revoke an agent token; its next request is refused. The owner's login only.
Give an agent token a new secret and expiry; the old secret is refused on its next request. Same gate as agent.token_issue.
List the live agent tokens as metadata only (never a secret). The owner's login only.
The full, unredacted record of one decision. Needs a Touch ID proof.
A summary of the audit log for a period: counts, denials, presence uses, chain check. Owner only; no values.
Recent audit records. For an agent the feed is redacted to id, action, time and actor.
Turn on unlocking with Touch ID: the vault key is sealed in this Mac's Secure Enclave.
Turn Touch ID unlock off.
Set the other names one entry answers to (the whole list, at most 8). A name or alias another entry has is refused. Human sessions only; no value is read or rewritten.
Create a new entry (one value or several fields). On a locked vault it is held in the pending tray.
Create 1 to 500 entries in one all-or-nothing call (used by credmgr import).
Entries that expire within N days (default 30; already expired included), across every node the caller may list or one node, soonest first. Names and dates only. Human sessions only.
One entry's metadata: field ids, labels, types, masking. Never a value.
Find an entry by its vault-wide short reference number. Only entries the caller could already list are found; anything else is not_found.
One entry's trail: the audit records that name it, oldest first, and its rotation and edit times. Never a value. Human sessions only.
Parsed .env pairs into one node: a dry run names every pair (new, exists, duplicate, empty, invalid), the write makes each pair its own entry with its own audit record. No answer carries a value.
Entry names and ids on one node. A human session also gets type, sensitivity and counts.

Move one entry to another node, re-sealed to that node's key in one crash-safe step; id, reference, name, aliases and expiry kept, grants on it revoked, Undo history dropped. Owner only, Admin on both nodes, a fresh second factor and a Touch ID check every time.
Soft-delete an entry into a 7-day recovery window.
Bring a removed entry back inside its recovery window.
Return field values. Waits for a human when the vault is locked or the node asks for a second factor.
Replace a value and keep the previous one as history.
Search names and aliases on one node. Names only, never values. The vault-wide search is the top-level search.
Set or clear an entry's expiry date (clear: true). Metadata only: the sealed value is not touched. Generation-checked like entry.update.
Which names on a node look like a candidate name (same letters with other separators or case, or one letter apart), and whether it is already taken. Writes nothing.

Replace one entry's tags (the whole set, at most 16; [] clears). Each is lower-cased, inner spaces become '-', letters, digits and - _ . : / only, 1-32 characters. Read like names; entry.list and entry.search filter one node by a tag. Human sessions only; no value is read or rewritten.
Undo a rotation, a field change or a removal, addressed by its audit record id.
Replace a field's value or the whole field list. Keeps no history.
Add fields to an entry.
Remove one field (never the last).
Change the order of an entry's fields. Presentation only.
Change one field's label, value, type or masking.

Create a grant between nodes, or from a node to one entry (read and/or reveal of that entry, which lists that entry only, one-way). Built up to its gate, then needs a Touch ID proof; refuses with presence_required without one.
List grants.
Revoke a grant.
The node tree the desktop app draws, filtered to what the caller may list.

Seal the passphrase file to this Mac's device key (made on first use, mode 0600, outside the vault folder). Needs the vault open and a recovery code, the way in on a new Mac. Idempotent. Refused to agents.

The machine lock's honest state: whether the passphrase file is sealed to a device key, whether this Mac holds that key, and that the tier is a key file (never the Secure Enclave). Owner login only; refused to agents before anything is read.
Turn the machine lock off: the passphrase file goes back to its plain form; the device key stays. A fresh second factor and Touch ID when they are set up. Refused to agents.
Write an encrypted backup archive under a passphrase the human chooses.
Diagnose and fix safe drift; optionally purge seals older than seven days. Rebuilding the registry needs a Touch ID proof.
Replace the root key and issue a new recovery code. Needs a Touch ID proof and a fresh second factor.
Check every envelope and manifest against its digest.

Keep one entry and fold others into it: their names become its aliases, their tags join its tags, and they are removed (each undoable for 7 days with entry.undo). A fresh second factor. Owner only, Admin on the node; one node at a time, never across a boundary; no value is ever returned.

Merge one open suggestion, only when its entries' values are all identical. A fresh second factor. Owner only, Admin on the node; one node at a time, never across a boundary; no value is ever returned.

Every open identical suggestion: a dry run that writes nothing unless apply is true (then a generation and a fresh second factor). Owner only, Admin on the node; one node at a time, never across a boundary; no value is ever returned.

Remember that a merge suggestion was rejected, so it is not suggested again; kept per node, sealed to the node's key. Owner only, Admin on the node; one node at a time, never across a boundary; no value is ever returned.
The merge suggestions a node remembers as dismissed, newest first, with their entries' names. Owner only, Admin on the node; one node at a time, never across a boundary; no value is ever returned.
Forget every dismissed merge suggestion on a node. Owner only, Admin on the node; one node at a time, never across a boundary; no value is ever returned.

Merge suggestions inside one node: identical values, a value in common, or names one letter apart, each with a key and the entry proposed to keep. Values are compared inside the broker under a key made for that call. Owner only, Admin on the node; one node at a time, never across a boundary; no value is ever returned.
Forget one dismissed merge suggestion, so it is suggested again. Owner only, Admin on the node; one node at a time, never across a boundary; no value is ever returned.
Create a project or sub-node, optionally with work folders.
An age-encrypted archive of a node, built inside the broker. Owner only; a fresh second factor and Touch ID; 2FA seeds are left out.
Begin giving one project a second factor of its own. Owner only.
Confirm a project's own second factor with one code; ten recovery codes of its own come back once.
Remove a project's own second factor: its fresh code and Touch ID, or the passphrase and the root recovery code.
Give a project's own code: it opens that project only, for five minutes, the owner included.
List nodes the caller may see.
Change a node's policy by partial patch. A patch that widens reach needs a Touch ID proof and refuses with presence_required without one.
A new key for one node, every file re-sealed to it. Owner only; a fresh second factor, a Touch ID check, one at a time.
Move a node under a different parent. Needs a Touch ID proof and a fresh second factor.
Restore a sealed node within seven days.
Seal a node: its entries move to Orphaned, re-encrypted to the cold key.
Bind directories to a node so an agent started inside is scoped to it.
Rename a node (the label only; the id never changes).
Read a node's markdown note. Needs the notes capability, which an agent scope never carries.
Write a node's markdown note. Needs the notes capability, which an agent scope never carries.
Permanently destroy sealed entries and the archives behind them. Owner only; the confirmation word, the count, a fresh second factor and Touch ID.
The sealed (Orphaned) entries, names only.
Read one sealed entry. Costs a fresh second factor and a Touch ID check every time; app only.
A single-use challenge for a Touch ID check on one operation. The app and the CLI ask for it themselves.
Enrol this Mac's Secure Enclave key. The first needs a fresh second factor; later ones need a Touch ID proof.
What this Mac can do for Touch ID and what is set up. The owner's login only.
Remove an enrolled presence key. Needs a Touch ID proof.
Search entry names across the nodes the caller can reach. Names only.
Find entries by what their field values contain; answers node, id and name only. Needs reveal; 12 a minute; never on a private node for an agent. Not an MCP tool.

Confirm it is you (Touch ID, or the vault passphrase) so the vault's 'confirm before showing secrets' rule lets this login see secrets for its trust window, or for one request. The owner's own login only; a wrong passphrase counts like a wrong unlock.
One setting in full, with its last ten recorded changes (each with the value it replaced).
The knowledge base for language models (docs/LLM_KB.md), generated from the settings table.

Every setting with its value, default, accepted values, what it is for, where it is stored, its risk and the rule for you. Pass node to include that project's settings (an agent only for a project it reaches).
Approve or deny an agent's request. Approving a change that weakens the vault needs a fresh confirmation (Touch ID or passphrase). The owner only.
The state of one agent request: pending, approved, denied or expired. Only its requester and the owner read it.
Every agent request waiting for or past the owner's decision, with the folder each was asked from. The owner only.
Put back the value a recorded change replaced, under the same rules as settings.set.
Change a setting. The owner: the rules the app always had. An agent: a cosmetic or stricter change applies at once; a weaker one waits for the owner's approval as a request.
The current six-digit code for a stored authenticator seed. Never the seed.
The stored seed itself. Refuses every caller without a Touch ID proof; no agent ever holds one, and no shipped client displays the answer.
Generate a random password (8 to 128 characters). The value is in the answer only: not stored, not audited.
Mark the anomaly alarm as seen, so vault.status stops counting it in anomaliesUnseen. Owner only.

Approve or deny an agent's waiting request. On a locked vault the passphrase (and the authenticator code) decide it; from a login, approving needs a Touch ID proof once a presence key is enrolled (denying never does).
Describe waiting agent requests. Works on a locked vault and decrypts nothing.

Apply every move of one tidy-up plan in one request: the exact moves the scan showed (entry, from, to, generation), each through entry.move's crash-safe commit, with one fresh second factor and one Touch ID check for the whole plan. Stops at the first move that fails and says what moved. Never returns a value. Owner only, Admin on every node it names.

The tidy-up scan: shared values, near-identical names, misfiled, weak, mistyped, expired, expiring and stale entries, each with a proposal; a move proposal carries the exact entry.move parameters. Writes nothing and never returns a value or a hash. Owner only, Admin on global.
Start setting up or replacing the vault's second factor.
Confirm the second factor with one code; issues ten recovery codes.
Reset the second factor with the passphrase and the root recovery code. Never unlocks.
Complete an unlock that asked for a code, or, from a logged-in session, open a five-minute step-up window.
Start creating the vault (only when none exists).
Finish creating the vault by retyping the recovery code.
Lock the vault and end every login.
Lock one node while the vault stays unlocked.
Unlock one node.
Accept a held entry into its node. This is the human's review step; an agent must not use it.
Discard a held entry. This is the human's review step; an agent must not use it.
List entries held in the review tray (names and counts, never values).

The passphrase is forgotten: open a locked vault with the recovery code, set a new passphrase and answer a new recovery code, shown once; the used code stops working. A second factor when one is on; never Touch ID. Refused to agents.
Change the vault passphrase (current and new). Replaces the root key and answers a new recovery code, shown once. A fresh second factor and Touch ID when they are set up.
Whether the vault is locked, initialised, and how many agent requests wait.
Unlock with the passphrase; returns a login token, or asks for a second-factor code.
The caller's own node, capabilities and the nodes it can reach.

broker_op_reach_meaning.mcp: Exposed as an MCP tool. This is the agent's whole interface.
broker_op_reach_meaning.capability_only: No MCP tool. The broker would accept the call from an agent-origin client that holds the capability, so an agent must not use it: several are the human's review or maintenance steps.
broker_op_reach_meaning.human_only: Needs Admin, the owner's login, the notes capability or presence, which an agent scope never carries.
broker_op_reach_meaning.bootstrap: Vault creation, unlock and lock operations that any local process may send and an agent never needs.

agent_access_meaning.none: No agent path. The feature is part of the app or the command line and an agent has no tool for it, or it is not relevant to an agent.
agent_access_meaning.read-only metadata: An agent can use it through an MCP tool to learn names, ids, labels, types, counts or its own boundary. No secret value is returned.
agent_access_meaning.read with approval: An agent can ask for secret values through an MCP tool. The broker answers at once only when the vault and node are unlocked and the node asks for no second factor; otherwise the request waits for a human (approval_pending or two_factor_required).
agent_access_meaning.read-write within its node: An agent can create or change data through an MCP tool, only inside the node it is scoped to, subject to that node's agent-access policy. Changes are audited, generation-checked and undoable.
agent_access_meaning.human only: Only a person can do this. An agent has no tool for it and the broker refuses an agent-origin caller.

usage: credmgr pending [--node <id>] [--json] (writes made while locked, awaiting review)
credmgr notes set <id> [--file <path>] (note text from the file or stdin; empty input is

credmgr node policy <id> --reason "..." [--agent-access read-write|read-only|none] [--require-two-factor never|reveal|always] [--lock-after-seconds <n>|none] [--json] [--private-names|--no-private-names] [--sibling-visibility shared|isolated] [--descendant-read|--no-descendant-read] [--security-level open|guarded|strict]
notes: A secret value is read from stdin and never travels as an argument.
credmgr mcp starts the MCP server; credmgr help lists every flag.
`credmgr unlock` prints a login token for a human's shell. It is not for agents.
